# Codebase audit against AGENTS documentation (2026-02-19 09:50Z)

_**User**_

Audit the entire codebase against all AGENTS documentation files.
Read every AGENTS file in the project root — AGENTS.md, AGENTS-SETUP.md, AGENTS-CONVENTIONS.md, AGENTS-PATTERNS.md, AGENTS-PATTERNS-REFERENCE.md, AGENTS-SECURITY.md, AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md, AGENTS-SEO.md, AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md, AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md, AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md, AGENTS-TESTING.md, and AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md — and then thoroughly scan the actual source code, configuration files, and project structure to compare what is documented versus what is implemented.
Produce a single comprehensive report with two clearly separated sections:
Documented but NOT implemented — Every convention, pattern, technique, configuration, or feature that the AGENTS files describe as part of the project but that is missing, incomplete, or incorrectly applied in the actual codebase. For each item, reference the specific AGENTS file and section where the claim is made, explain what is expected, and describe what you found (or didn't find) in the code.
Documented AND implemented — Every convention, pattern, technique, configuration, or feature that the AGENTS files describe and that is correctly present in the codebase. For each item, briefly reference where in the code it is fulfilled.
Be exhaustive: check project structure, naming conventions, file-system conventions, JSDoc/documentation style, Container-Presentational pattern, Server Action hardening, Data Access Facade, error boundaries, auth configuration, CSP/headers, input validation, CSRF protection, metadata/OG/sitemap/robots, React Compiler usage, code splitting, loading states, bundle optimization, accessibility landmarks, skip link, form accessibility, animation patterns (Motion, NumberFlow, tw-animate-css), testing setup (Vitest, Playwright), mocking strategies, CI configuration, Drizzle schema conventions, Zod validation schemas, and anything else the AGENTS files mention.
Do not propose fixes or create a plan of action — only report findings.
